channel.title: Papers on Kevin Schoenholzer
channel.description: Recent content in Papers on Kevin Schoenholzer

item.title: Cumulative advantage in the early career: Within-person dynamics of the graduate income advantage in five countries
item.description: Cumulative advantage in income position is a feature of the early career, not of the career as a whole.

item.title: Welfare state policy and educational inequality: a cross-national multicohort study
item.description: Findings provide evidence of the mixed role of welfare state policies for social inequality in student achievement.

item.title: Does Rising Cohort Achievement Narrow the Tertiary Earnings Gap? Evidence on Earnings Rank from 36 Countries
item.description: Many of today’s working-age cohorts scored higher in school-age assessments than the cohorts before them. I ask whether such gains go with a smaller earnings gap between tertiary graduates and non-graduates. I link a harmonised cohort achievement index to PIAAC data for 126,590 adults in 36 countries.

item.title: Softening the binary divide: sorting and outcomes in the multi-pathway Swiss tertiary system
item.description: Switzerland kept vocational and academic higher education apart and built regulated bridges between the two sectors. We ask what this strategy delivers for social-origin sorting and for graduate outcomes. We use four cohorts of the Swiss Graduate Survey and a typology of eight graduate pathways.

item.title: Narrowed but Stable: Decomposing the SES Gradient in Tertiary Educational Expectations Across 33 OECD Countries, 2003-2022
item.description: Students from advantaged families expect a tertiary degree more often than other students. I ask how much of this gap runs through achievement, and whether the gap changed as tertiary education expanded. I use five PISA cycles from 2003 to 2022 for 33 OECD countries, and three TIMSS cycles.

item.title: When the Mother Holds the Degree: Parents’ Education and Children’s Skills in 79 Education Systems, 2003 to 2022
item.description: Working paper. In 79 education systems, 2003 to 2022, the PISA score difference between children whose mother alone holds a tertiary degree and children whose father alone holds one rose by 3.0 points per decade in mathematics and 3.9 in reading.

item.title: Educational Expansion and Shifts in the Social Origins of Tertiary Graduates
item.description: Educational expansion changes attainment chances and raises the share of each cohort with tertiary-educated parents. We ask how the social origins of tertiary graduates changed across cohorts born between 1948 and 1992. We compare six countries with harmonised household panel data.

item.title: Legitimizing Education-based Earnings Differences in an Era of Educational Expansion: Evidence from 28 Countries
item.description: Do people believe that education should determine how much a person earns? We ask whether this belief changed as education expanded, and whether it depends on a person’s own educational position. We use four waves of the International Social Survey Programme, 1992 to 2019, for 28 countries.

item.title: Social Origin, Institutional Sorting, and Student Experience in Swiss Higher Education
item.description: Social origin shapes where students study and how they fare during their studies. I ask whether unequal experience reflects sorting between institutions or persists among students at the same institution. I use four waves of the Swiss Survey on the Social and Economic Situation of Students (2013 to 2024).

item.title: Creating effective flood warnings: A framework from a critical review
item.description: A systematic review of risk perception and warning communication for flood early warning systems, with a framework for creating effective warnings.
